nodes.title: Rate of Reaction & Rate Law
points: Average Rate: r_avg = −Δ[R]/Δt = +Δ[P]/Δt. Instantaneous Rate: r_inst = −d[R]/dt = +d[P]/dt.
For generalized reaction aA + bB ⟶ cC + dD:
Rate Law: Experimentally determined equation relating reaction rate to molar concentrations of reactants:
Rate = k [A]^x [B]^y, where k is rate constant (specific reaction rate), and x, y are orders with respect to A and B.
Rate constant k is independent of concentration; depends only on temperature and catalyst.

nodes.title: Order vs Molecularity & Pseudo-First Order
points: Order of Reaction: Sum of exponents of concentration terms in the rate law (n = x + y). Determined experimentally only. Can be zero, fractional, integer, or negative.

Molecularity of Reaction: Number of reactant species colliding simultaneously in an elementary step. Theoretical concept. Always a positive whole integer (1, 2, or 3); CANNOT be zero, fractional, or > 3.
Pseudo-First Order Reaction: A higher-order reaction that follows first-order kinetics because one reactant is present in large excess:
1. Acid hydrolysis of ester: CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O(excess) ⟶[H⁺] CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH (Rate = k' [ester][H₂O] = k [ester]).
2. Inversion of cane sugar: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ + H₂O(excess) ⟶ C₆H₁₂O₆ + C₆H₁₂O₆.

formulas.label: Order of reaction
formulas.expr: n = x + y (experimental sum of exponents)

nodes.title: Zero Order Reactions
points: Definition: Reaction rate is independent of reactant concentration: Rate = k [A]⁰ = k.
Unit of rate constant k: mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹ (or mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹).
Integrated Rate Law: k = ([A]₀ − [A]_t) / t ⟹ [A]_t = [A]₀ − k t.
Half-Life Period (t_½): Time required for concentration to decrease to half its initial value:
t_½ = [A]₀ / (2k). Notice: t_½ is directly proportional to initial concentration [A]₀.
Examples: Decomposition of NH₃ on hot Pt surface; Photochemical H₂ + Cl₂ ⟶ 2HCl; 2HI ⟶[Au] H₂ + I₂.

nodes.title: First Order Reactions: Integrated Rate Law & Half-Life
points: Definition: Reaction rate is directly proportional to the first power of reactant concentration: Rate = k [A].
Unit of rate constant k: s⁻¹ or min⁻¹ (independent of concentration units!).
Integrated Rate Law: k = (2.303 / t) log₁₀([A]₀ / [A]_t) = (2.303 / t) log₁₀[a / (a − x)].
Exponential Form: [A]_t = [A]₀ e^(−kt).
Half-Life Period (t_½): t_½ = 0.693 / k.
CRITICAL: Half-life of a first-order reaction is strictly INDEPENDENT of initial concentration [A]₀!
First Order Gas Phase Reaction (A(g) ⟶ B(g) + C(g)): k = (2.303 / t) log₁₀[P_i / (2P_i − P_t)], where P_i is initial pressure and P_t is total pressure at time t.

nodes.title: Graphical Representations in Kinetics
points: Zero Order Graphs:
1. [A]_t vs t: Straight line with negative slope = −k and y-intercept = [A]₀.
2. Rate vs [A]: Horizontal straight line (slope = 0).
3. t_½ vs [A]₀: Straight line passing through origin (slope = 1/2k).
First Order Graphs:
1. log₁₀[A]_t vs t: Straight line with negative slope = −k / 2.303 and intercept = log₁₀[A]₀.
2. log₁₀([A]₀ / [A]_t) vs t: Straight line passing through origin with positive slope = k / 2.303.
3. Rate vs [A]: Straight line passing through origin with slope = k.
4. t_½ vs [A]₀: Horizontal line (independent of [A]₀).

nodes.title: Collision Theory & Activation Energy
points: Collision Theory: Reaction occurs when reactant molecules collide. Rate = Z_AB · f, where Z_AB is collision frequency and f is fraction of effective collisions.
Two Requirements for Effective Collisions:
1. Energy Barrier: Colliding molecules must possess minimum kinetic energy called Threshold Energy: E_threshold = E_reactants + E_a.
Activation Energy (E_a): Minimum extra energy required by reactants to form activated complex: E_a = E_threshold − E_reactants.
2. Orientation Barrier: Colliding molecules must have proper spatial orientation at the moment of collision to break existing bonds and form new ones.
Activated Complex / Transition State: High-energy, unstable arrangement of atoms with partial bonds.

nodes.title: Arrhenius Equation & Temperature Dependence
points: Arrhenius Equation: Expresses quantitative relationship between temperature and rate constant: k = A · e^(−E_a / RT).
Where: A = Frequency factor (pre-exponential factor), E_a = activation energy (J/mol), R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, T = temperature in Kelvin.
Logarithmic Form: log₁₀ k = log₁₀ A − [E_a / (2.303 R T)].
Plot of log₁₀ k vs 1/T is a straight line with slope = −E_a / (2.303 R) and y-intercept = log₁₀ A.
Two Temperature Formula: log₁₀(k₂ / k₁) = [E_a / (2.303 R)] · [(T₂ − T₁) / (T₁ T₂)].
Temperature Coefficient: Rate of most reactions roughly DOUBLES or TRIPLES for every 10 °C rise in temperature (k_(T+10) / k_T ≈ 2 to 3).

formulas.label: Arrhenius linear form
formulas.expr: log₁₀ k = log₁₀ A − [E_a / (2.303 R T)]

nodes.title: Effect of Catalyst on Reaction Rate
points: A catalyst increases reaction rate by providing an alternative reaction pathway with a LOWER Activation Energy (E_a).
Because E_a is lowered, a much larger fraction of colliding molecules possesses kinetic energy ≥ E_a, exponentially increasing rate constant k.
Key Catalyst Properties:
1. Catalyst DOES NOT alter ΔH, ΔU, or ΔG of the reaction.
2. Catalyst DOES NOT alter the equilibrium constant K_eq; it accelerates both forward and backward reactions equally, helping reach equilibrium faster.
3. A catalyst cannot initiate a non-spontaneous reaction.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Derivations & Definitions
points: Board Favourite #1: Derive integrated rate law for a first-order reaction: k = (2.303 / t) log₁₀([A]₀ / [A]_t) and show t_½ = 0.693 / k.
Board Favourite #2: Derive integrated rate expression for a gas-phase first-order reaction: A(g) ⟶ B(g) + C(g).
Board Favourite #3: Distinguish between Order and Molecularity of a reaction (4 key points).
Board Favourite #4: State Arrhenius equation and derive: log₁₀(k₂ / k₁) = [E_a / (2.303 R)] [(T₂ − T₁) / (T₁ T₂)].
Board Favourite #5: Define: (1) Half-life period, (2) Pseudo-first order reaction, (3) Activation energy, (4) Rate law.

nodes.title: MHT-CET Kinetics Shortcuts, Unit Hacks & Half-Life Tricks
points: General Unit of Rate Constant k: (mol L⁻¹)^(1 − n) s⁻¹, where n is order of reaction.
• Zero order: mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹; First order: s⁻¹; Second order: L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹.
Half-Life Proportionality Rule: t_½ ∝ 1 / [A]₀^(n − 1).
• Zero order: t_½ ∝ [A]₀; First order: t_½ ∝ [A]₀⁰ (independent); Second order: t_½ ∝ 1 / [A]₀.
First Order Percentage Completion Shortcuts:
• t_75% = 2 × t_50% (75% completed in 2 half-lives).
• t_87.5% = 3 × t_50% (87.5% completed in 3 half-lives).
Arrhenius Graph Slope Hack: Slope of log₁₀ k vs 1/T is −E_a / (2.303 R) ⟹ E_a = −2.303 × R × Slope.
